title: Why West Africa Is Offering Citizenship to the African Diaspora | The Six, Ep. 1
lede: Since 2016, Ghana, Sierra Leone, Benin and Guinea-Bissau have granted at least 1,213 citizenships to descendants of enslaved Africans. Each country wrote different rules, and those rules are deciding which programs last. This episode traces how the African Union's Sixth Region went from a 2003 charter amendment to a passport.
keyPoints: Ghana (834 grants) acts by executive decision. It suspended its process in February 2026 after adding a DNA rule and a tenfold fee increase, then reinstated it without the DNA test.
Benin is the only country with a dedicated law (No. 2024-31). Nationality through it does not include the right to vote or run for office.
Sierra Leone verifies ancestry by DNA test and offers a $100,000 investment route for people of African heritage.
Guinea-Bissau grants citizenship by decree to descendants of specific ethnic groups. Its process is paused amid political instability, with a general election set for December 6.
